transcript.statement: The system must adhere to the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications (RES-01) to ensure safety and compliance in autonomous operations. Implementing a multi-layer safety architecture (RES-02) is critical for accountability and effective response to failures. Executing Minimal Risk Maneuvers (RES-03) within 5 seconds is essential to ensure safety in critical situations. Continuous monitoring of ODD compliance (RES-04) and timely HMI warnings (RES-05) strengthen user trust and safety. It is vital to prioritize passenger safety over comfort and speed during emergency maneuvers (RES-06) to fulfill our ethical responsibilities. Lastly, documenting all safety decisions (RES-07) is necessary for regulatory compliance and accountability.

transcript.statement: To ensure the highest level of safety and reliability in autonomous driving, the system must implement a multi-layer safety architecture (SAF-01) and execute Minimal Risk Maneuvers (SAF-02) within a strict timeframe to prevent accidents. transcript.statement: The integrity and security of user data are paramount in autonomous driving systems. Implementing end-to-end data encryption (TRU-01) and role-based access control (TRU-02) ensures that only authorized personnel can access sensitive information, protecting user privacy. Logging all access and modifications (TRU-03) is essential for auditability, enabling us to trace unauthorized access. Incorporating data anonymization techniques (TRU-04) safeguards user identities, while regular security audits (TRU-05) help identify vulnerabilities proactively. Secure remote software updates (TRU-06) are crucial for maintaining system integrity against malware threats. Informing users about data practices (TRU-07) builds trust and compliance with regulations.

To achieve optimal performance in autonomous driving, the system must prioritize efficiency in path planning and operational responsiveness. Optimizing travel time (EFF-01) is crucial for enhancing user experience, while maintaining a jerk value below 0.5 m/s³ (EFF-02) ensures passenger comfort without compromising safety. The ability to execute Minimal Risk Maneuvers within 5 seconds (EFF-03) is vital for safety and performance. Continuous monitoring of ODD compliance with low latency (EFF-04) enables real-time adjustments. Achieving a high success rate in optimal speed profile generation (EFF-05) is important for overall system efficiency, and utilizing iterative quadratic programming efficiently (EFF-06) is necessary for handling complex scenarios. Lastly, prioritizing smoothness during emergency maneuvers (EFF-07) is essential for ensuring passenger comfort and system reliability.

requirements.text: The system shall maintain compliance with the Apollo Pilot Safety Report and EM Motion Planner specifications at all operational times.
The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture that guarantees active monitoring and response to critical system failures.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting a critical failure to ensure safe stopping.
The system shall continuously monitor and enforce compliance with its defined Operational Design Domain.
The system shall provide timely HMI warnings to request human takeover whenever ODD compliance is at risk.
The system shall minimize jerk during maneuvers while allowing dynamic adjustments based on situational severity.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints reliably.
The system shall establish emergency protocols that minimize energy usage during critical failures.
The system shall implement end-to-end data encryption for all user data transmitted.
The system shall enforce role-based access control to restrict user permissions based on their role.
The system shall log all access and modifications to critical data for auditability purposes.
The system shall implement a mechanism for secure remote software updates to protect against malware.
The system shall minimize energy consumption during operation by optimizing path and speed profiles.
The system shall achieve high energy recovery efficiency during braking maneuvers.
